column3: The palace of the Ming and Qing emperors for almost 500 years, with nearly a thousand buildings behind red walls and a moat. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
One of the largest public squares in the world, with the Gate of Heavenly Peace on the north and the Great Hall of the People on the west.
Where Ming and Qing emperors prayed for good harvests. Its round, blue-tiled Hall of Prayer stands on a three-tiered white marble terrace.
A lake and a hill garden that served as the Qing court's summer retreat, with a long painted corridor, a marble boat and temples.
One of the oldest imperial gardens in China, built around a lake with a white pagoda on an island. You can rent a boat in summer.
An artificial hill just north of the Forbidden City, and the best place to see the palace roofs spread out in a golden sea.
The best-known part of the Great Wall, with steep Ming-era stairs and watchtowers that climb the ridge. It is about an hour from Beijing.
A restored stretch of the Great Wall in green hills, quieter than Badaling, with cable cars and even a toboggan ride down.
The National Stadium, built for the 2008 Olympics. Its steel lattice looks like a bird's nest woven from twigs.
The swimming center of the 2008 Olympics, wrapped in a skin of blue bubbles, which is now also a water park.
A big Tibetan Buddhist temple that was once a prince's home. Its tallest hall holds a huge Buddha carved from a single tree trunk.
A vast museum on the east side of Tiananmen Square, telling the story of China's history and displaying thousands of treasures.
An old hutong lane with cafés, souvenir shops and street snacks, always busy with visitors and locals.
A group of lakes with old courtyard houses, willow trees, bars and boats. People skate on it in winter.
The ruins of a vast imperial garden that was burned by Anglo-French troops in 1860. Broken marble pillars remain among the lakes.
The burial ground of thirteen Ming emperors in a valley north of Beijing, reached along a Sacred Way lined with stone animals.
A former factory complex, now filled with galleries, studios and cafés, where old industrial buildings meet contemporary art.
A Ming-era observatory on the old city wall, with large bronze instruments that were used to track the stars and planets.
Roast duck with thin, crisp skin, carved at the table and eaten rolled in a pancake with scallions, cucumber and sweet bean sauce. It is Beijing's most famous dish.
Hand-pulled noodles topped with a thick fried soybean paste and fresh sliced vegetables. This is the everyday noodle of old Beijing.
A sour, fermented mung bean drink with a strong smell, eaten with pickles. Many visitors find it tough, but it is a true Beijing taste.
A sticky rice roll filled with red bean paste and rolled in soybean flour, named for the cloud of flour that flies up like a donkey rolling in the dust.
Hawthorn berries on a stick, coated in a shiny layer of hard sugar, a winter street snack. The sour fruit meets the sweet candy.
Thin slices of lamb are swished in a pot of simmering water, then dipped in sesame sauce. It is a favorite winter meal in Beijing.
An old Beijing dish of pork offal and fried tofu simmered in a rich broth with flatbread. A taste for the brave.
A soft, sticky rice ball filled with sweet nuts and sugar, a traditional snack of Beijing that was once eaten at festivals.
Peking opera combines singing, speech, acrobatics and martial arts. The actors wear painted faces and rich costumes that show their role in the story.
A comedy talk show for two performers who trade jokes and puns, quick and clever. It is a classic of Beijing and Tianjin.
Cloisonné is a craft in which thin copper wires are filled with colored enamel and fired, to make vases and bowls with a deep blue glow.
A traditional home with four buildings arranged around a central courtyard, set along a hutong, the heart of old Beijing family life.
A giant Ferris wheel that rises from a bridge over the Hai River, with a view of the old city and the river from the top.
A pedestrian street with old-style shopfronts, selling crafts, calligraphy, clay figures and Tianjin snacks.
A neighborhood of Italian-style houses and piazzas from the days when Italy had a concession in Tianjin, now full of cafés.
A mansion whose outside walls are covered with more than 400 million pieces of old porcelain, glass and jade, and even ancient vases.
Tianjin's most famous steamed buns have a fine pleated top and a juicy pork filling. The name means Dog Doesn't Care, from a nickname of the founder.
A thin crepe fried with egg, brushed with sauce and rolled around a crisp fried cracker. It is Tianjin's favorite street breakfast.
Twisted fried dough sticks, crisp and sweet, and a famous Tianjin snack that is sold in boxes as a gift.
A sticky rice cake fried until golden and filled with sweet bean paste. It is named after the alley where it was first made.
A Tianjin breakfast soup of strips of mung bean pancake in a savory sauce with sesame paste and fermented bean curd.
A family of clay-figure artists whose delicate, lifelike hand-modeled statues have been made in Tianjin for about 180 years.
Brightly colored New Year prints from Yangliuqing, with cheerful scenes of children, fish and good-luck symbols, printed by hand.
The oldest large stone arch bridge in China, built around 600 CE. Its low arch has survived floods and earthquakes for 1,400 years.
An old walled town with temples, pagodas and a Buddha statue, once an important northern city.
A Buddhist temple in Zhengding with a 22-meter bronze statue of the Thousand-Armed Guanyin, which was cast in the Song dynasty.
A flatbread stuffed with braised donkey meat, a famed specialty of Zhengding. The sandwich is crisp outside and rich inside.
A sesame flatbread baked against the wall of a jar-shaped oven, making it crisp and fragrant.
A huge imperial garden and palace in the hills of Chengde, where Qing emperors spent the summer and held court. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
A big Tibetan-style temple, modeled on the Potala Palace in Lhasa, built by Emperor Qianlong in the 18th century.
A tall rock that looks like a hammer, standing on a hillside above Chengde, a local symbol.
A forest and grassland that planters turned from a barren land into a green refuge across decades, a model of ecological work.
A sweet, milky drink made from almonds, and a popular local drink that is served cold.
A crisp baked bun filled with braised donkey meat, which is a well-loved comfort food in Hebei.
A strong fortress at a pass where the Great Wall meets the sea, nicknamed the First Pass Under Heaven.
The place where the Great Wall meets the Bohai Sea, and its end looks like a dragon's head dipping into the water.
A seaside resort on the Bohai coast with beaches, villas and sea breezes, a summer escape for many decades.
A traditional banquet of eight bowls of local dishes, served at festivals and weddings in the Shanhaiguan area.
Crabs, shrimp and shellfish from the Bohai Sea, cooked fresh in the seaside restaurants of Qinhuangdao.
A large wetland of reeds, lotus flowers and little lakes, where you travel by boat through narrow channels.
A burial ground of four Qing emperors, in a pine forest, with red walls and stone gates.
The classic donkey meat bun from Baoding, with a crisp, golden bread and soft, savory meat.
Fish from the lake, stewed in a pot with local herbs, a taste of the wetland.
A large tomb complex of Qing emperors, including Qianlong and Empress Dowager Cixi, set in the hills at the foot of Mount Changrui.
A small, round flatbread like a chess piece, baked with sesame seeds, a Tangshan favorite.
Millet from the hills of Wu'an, which cooks into a fragrant, golden porridge.
Noodles made from naked oats, rolled and steamed into small cylinders, a staple of the cool highlands in Zhangjiakou.
A spiced sausage made by the Hui community of Dachang, with a rich, savory taste.
A buttery, flaky pastry from Neiqiu, a sweet treat with a long tradition.
Small jujubes that show golden threads of sugar when you break them in half, among the best dates in China.
Chicken stewed with spices in a pot at the table, a favorite meal in Cangzhou.
A strong, clear spirit made in Hengshui for centuries, with a sharp and clean taste.
